substantive_delta: The candidate realizes a delay L=lcm(ell_i) using only sum_i ell_i clock states and one k-element packet. An all-word singleton-image invariant preserves the global k bound. A port-separated queue potential forces m+1 disjoint full-period events even with resets and simultaneous reforks. Choosing pairwise-coprime lengths for every sufficiently large n yields Omega_k(n^(k+1)) for every k>=2, matching the known upper bound even for binary strongly connected automata.
why_nonroutine: CRT alone supplies only n^k; the verified deterministic tail lemma spends L physical states for an L delay. Neither supplies reusable nondeterministic clock compression with an unchanged global row bound or rules out shortcuts when that compressed delay is shared by a linear-size queue. The candidate proves those missing properties by a new invariant and exact potential. This is a substantive full-hierarchy construction relative to the verified prior work, not a k=1 rediscovery, an isolated finite witness, or a routine application whose hypotheses already contain the result.
significance: The theorem resolves the complete fixed-k interpretation of the published MFCS 2025 tightness question, with explicit positive constants and a construction at every n beyond a stated threshold. It establishes the optimal polynomial exponent at every nondeterministic image-bound level while retaining binary alphabet and strong connectivity. This has clear extremal automata and bounded-support mortality value; no claim of venue acceptance or optimal leading constants is made.
